Geostatistics — Precipitation and Air Pollution Interpolation

The challenge

Environmental data is always collected at discrete point locations, but decision-making requires continuous spatial coverage. This project tackled two real-world interpolation problems: monthly precipitation across Finland (Finnish Meteorological Institute) and air pollutant concentrations across Europe (European Environment Agency).

The approach

For precipitation, spatial autocorrelation was first analysed to understand the data structure, then Kriging and Inverse Distance Weighting were applied and compared against a reference raster surface. For air pollution, point measurements were converted to continuous raster maps using selected interpolation methods guided by analysis of the dataset's spatial properties.

Key outcomes

Monthly precipitation surface interpolated across Finland using Kriging and IDW

European air pollutant concentrations mapped from point data to continuous raster

Spatial autocorrelation analysis used to guide and validate interpolation method selection
